notes.meaning: God finished making the heavens, the earth, and everything that fills them. All of creation was complete, so nothing new needed to be added to the universe. We can trust that God's work in creation was entirely whole and perfect.

God stopped His creative work on the seventh day because He had finished what He set out to do. He did not stop because He was tired, since God never grows weary. Instead, He ceased working to show His satisfaction with what He had made and to give people a pattern for their own week.

God declared the seventh day special and set it apart as holy. He made it a day of rest and worship to mark the completion of His creation. This pattern reminds us to take time to honor God and rest from our daily labor.

This statement introduces the detailed story of how God shaped the earth and cared for humanity. The name LORD God appears here for the first time, combining His personal covenant name, Yahweh, with His title as Creator, Elohim. It shows that the mighty Maker of the universe is also a caring God who relates closely to His people.

Cultivated plants and grain had not yet grown because God had not sent rain, and there was no human being to farm the soil. Wild growth and farmed fields require human care and regular water. From the start, human work was meant to be a natural part of caring for the earth.

Instead of rain falling from clouds above, underground water welled up to soak the ground. This moisture kept the soil damp and ready for plant life. God faithfully provided what the earth needed to thrive even before the weather patterns of later times began.

God shaped the first man out of the dust of the earth, just like a potter shapes clay. Then He personally breathed life into man's nostrils, making him a living person with a body and spirit. This unique gift shows that human beings have a special worth and a personal bond with their Maker.

God prepared a lush garden in a region called Eden toward the east and put the man there to live. The name Eden means a place of delight and rich fertility. God provided a safe and beautiful home where humanity could enjoy fellowship with Him.

God made all kinds of trees grow in the garden, giving Adam both beautiful scenery and delicious food. In the center stood the tree of life, offering eternal fellowship, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. God surrounded man with every good gift and gave him the freedom to trust His wisdom.

A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden and keep it green and fruitful. After passing through Eden, the water divided into four major streams. God's abundant provision in the garden was rich enough to flow out and refresh the surrounding world.

The first river was called Pishon, which flowed around the land of Havilah. That region was famous for its fine gold, fragrant resin, and precious onyx stones. These riches show how bountiful and beautiful God made the land surrounding the garden.

The second river was the Gihon, flowing around Cush, while the third was the Tigris, running east of Assyria, alongside the fourth river, the Euphrates. Two of these rivers remain well-known landmarks in the ancient world. Their mention anchors the biblical story in real geographical history.

The Lord placed Adam in the Garden of Eden to tend the plants and guard the land. Even before sin entered the world, God gave man good and satisfying work to do. Working with our hands and caring for what God gives us is an honorable calling.

God told the man he could freely eat fruit from almost every tree in the garden. However, God strictly warned him not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, saying disobedience would bring certain death. This command tested whether humanity would trust God's boundary and remain loyal to Him.

differ.view: Adam was placed under a covenant of works, where perfect obedience would secure eternal life, while disobedience brought death to him and his descendants.
This command was a straightforward test of human trust and moral obedience, rather than a formal legal covenant of works.

notes.meaning: God declared that it was not good for man to be isolated and by himself. He promised to make a partner who would perfectly fit Adam and help him carry out his life's purpose. God created human beings to live in loving relationship with one another.

God brought the birds and land animals to Adam to see what he would name them. Adam carefully studied each creature and gave it a name, showing his authority over them, but none of them was an equal companion for him. This exercise helped Adam realize his need for a partner of his own kind.

God put Adam into a deep, peaceful sleep so he would feel no pain. He took a rib from Adam's side, closed up the flesh, and carefully fashioned it into a woman before presenting her to the man. She was taken from his side so she would stand beside him as an equal partner to be loved and protected.

When Adam saw the woman, he burst into joyful praise because she was made of the very same bone and flesh as himself. He called her woman because she was taken out of man. Her arrival brought him total delight in finding someone who shared his human nature.

This passage explains that a man leaves his mother and father to join himself permanently to his wife, forming a new family as one flesh. Marriage is a holy bond created by God that takes priority over all other family ties. God designed marriage to be a lifelong union of love, faithfulness, and deep unity.

The man and his wife were completely unclad, yet they felt no shame or embarrassment. Because sin had not yet touched their hearts, they lived in pure trust, innocence, and openness with each other and with God. True purity brings freedom and peaceful confidence without any fear or guilt.
